DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 06 s. 2022 JAN 19 2022 Mr. JOSE RUEDA Director, Ion Real Estate Development Corporation 26th Floor, Twenty-Four Seven McKinley 24th Street corner 7th Avenue Bonifacio Global City, Taguig Dear Mr. Rueda: This refers to your undated Letter, forwarded by the Office of the President to this Department, requesting for a legal opinion on the propriety of the restrictions imposed by Punong Barangay Thomas Raymond U. Lising (PB Lising) of Barangay San Antonio, Pasig City (Barangay), as follows: (I) Whether or not it is legal for Punong Barangay Lising to bar IREDC representative/s form entering the property they own; and (2) Whether or not entering Barangay San Antonio, Pasig City with the intention of having a dialogue and conducting negotiations with informal settlers is considered as a "Barangay Activity" that requires an activity clearance from the Barangay. Per your undated Letter, the facts and circumstances relating to your queries are as follows: • Ion Real Estate Development Corporation, (IREDC) is the registered owner of three (3) parcels of land located at the Barangay (Properties). • Beginning 2021, several persons, including members of the Barangay council, illegally entered the property and built structures thereon. IREDC thus sought an audience with PB Lising in order to discuss the possibility of removing the informal settlers amicably. • They were allegedly originally scheduled by Barangay Secretary Analyn Soropia (Ms. Soropia) to meet with PB Lising at 2:00PM on 05 May 2021. Upon IREDC's arrival at the said date and time, Ms. Soropia insisted that they were late and, as a result thereof, PB Lising refused to see them. • On 24 May 2021, IREDC sent PB Lising a Letter of same date requesting that a dialogue be conducted between IREDC and the informal settlers. IREDC further requested that PB Lising intervene in the dialogue pursuant to his position as the barangay chairperson and ex-officio chair of the lupong tagapamayapa. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

• When IREDC attempted to serve the Letter personally to the informal settlers, they were prevented by members of the San Antonio Pasig Barangay Police Force (Barangay Police Force). As per IREDC, they were told by the Barangay Police Force that they were acting under the directive of PB Lising. • IREDC attempted to secure the areas of the Properties which remained unoccupied. They were, however, again prevented by the Barangay Police Force pursuant to the orders of PB Lising. • PB Lising met with the representatives of IREDC once via Zoom where he stated that the informal settlers are not claiming ownership of the Properties. There was, however, no discussion on the possible settlement between the informal settlers and IREDC. As of date, IREDC's requested dialogue has not materialized. • On 16 June 2021, IREDC's representative Mr. Thomas Siy III requested for assistance from the Department's NCR Regional Office (DILG-NCR) in the alleged inaction and harassment exhibited by the Barangay. His concem was forwarded by DILG-NCR to DILG Pasig City. • Based on the Letter dated 14 July 2021, DILG- NCR recommended that IREDC file the appropriate case with the Office of the Ombudsman, which IREDC duly filed on 25 June 2021. DILG Pasig likewise coordinated with PB Lising after receipt of the IREDC's concem. With due respect, this Department is of the opinion that: (a) the Barangay cannot bar persons from entering their own property; and (b) IREDC does need the permission of the barangay to conduct negotiations with the informal settlers. This Department notes that the subject Properties are private property, not of public nature. As such, the rules provided under Republic Act No. 386, otherwise known as the New Civil Code (NCC) shall apply. The pertinent provisions therein are: •Article 427. Ownership may be exercised over things or rights. (n) Article 428. The owner has the right to enjoy and dispose of a thing, without other limitations than those established by law. The owner has also a right of action against the holder and possessor of the thing in order to recover it (348a) Article 429. The owner or lawful possessor of a thing has the right to exclude any person from the enjoyment and disposal thereof. For this purpose, he may use such force as may be reasonably necessary to repel or prevent an actual or threatened unlawful physical invasion or usurpation of his property. (n)' In the case of the Heirs ofAlfredo Cullado vs. Dominic Gutierrezi, the Supreme Court listed the attributes of ownership: In an accion reivindicatoria, the cause of action of the plaintiff is to recover possession by virtue of his ownership of the land subject of the dispute. This follows that universe of rights conferred to the owner of property, or more commonly known as the attributes of ownership-32 In classical Roman law terms, they are: f. Jus gessldendi or the riqht to po-#ess; Heirs of Cullado vs. Dominic Gutierrez, G.R. No. 212938 dated 30 July 2019. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

2. Jus utendi or the riqht to use and enioy: 3. Jus fruendi or the right to the fruits; 4. Jus accessionis or right to accessories; 5. Jus abutendi or the right to consume the thing by its use; 6. Jus disponendi or the right to dispose or alienate; and 7. Jus vindicandi or the riaht to vindicate or recover.2 Based on the foregoing, the owner of private property has the right to enter and use the same subject to limitations stated under the law. An example of a limitation is Article 429 of the NCC — that the owner may use necessary force to prevent an actual or threatened unlawful usurpation of his property. Once a person is already occupying the property, however, the owner may not take the law into his own hands and forcibly evict the former.3 The owner must file the proper action for forcible entry or unlawful detainer. Verily, IREDC is the owner of the Properties which are classified as private properties. They have the right enter the same subject to the limitations stated under the law. The Barangay may not interfere with such right unless provided by law. Consequently, this Department is of the opinion that IREDC may not be barred from entering the Property by Barangay officials. This Department further confirms that IREDC, as the owner, likewise has the right to initiate actions to recover possession of the Properties from the informal settlers. Such recovery of private property may be done by the parties, who are all private persons, through either judicial means such as the filing for a case for ejectment, or extrajudicial settlement or negotiations. The requested dialogue by IREDC with the informal settlers, at present, remain to be a private affair between themselves in furtherance of an extrajudicial settlement of the issue. At the present stage, this level deems it unnecessary to require the Barangay's permission to settle a private matter. The Barangay, however, is not precluded from assisting should a party request for the same, and to act as the Lupon Tagapamayapa when the proper complaint is filed. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same and rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts.
